title: Cannabis Cookies Recipe: Sugar or Chocolate Chip
h1: Easy Cannabis Cookies, Two Ways (Sugar or Chocolate Chip)
metaDescription: One cannabutter dough that bakes into sugar or chocolate chip cookies, with a simple per-cookie dose calculation plus storage and labeling tips.
excerpt: One flexible cannabutter dough, two classic cookies, and the math up front: your butter's strength divided by the number of cookies.
keyTakeaways: Work out the dose before you bake: the mg in the cannabutter you use, divided by the number of cookies.
Blend cannabutter with plain butter to bring each cookie down to a lower dose.
Shape 12 cookies from each half of the dough, so chips don't change anyone's dose.
A cookie's effects may take 2 hours to arrive, so wait before reaching for a second.
Store them labeled and airtight, away from everyday snacks, kids and pets.
body:
This cannabis cookies recipe starts with one cannabutter dough. Bake half as sugar cookies and fold chocolate chips into the rest, or go all one way. The step that matters most happens before the oven: working out how much THC ends up in each cookie.

## Dosing and safety: do the math before you bake

Each cookie's dose is the cannabutter's total THC split across the batch. This recipe takes 8 tablespoons of butter and makes about 24 cookies. The table shows how blending in plain butter changes things if your cannabutter tops out near 39 mg per tablespoon, the full-cup figure in our [cannabutter recipe](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) example; butter that strains out to less than a cup runs stronger:

| Cannabutter | Plain butter | THC per cookie, at most |
|---|---|---|
| 1 tablespoon | 7 tablespoons | about 1.6 mg |
| 2 tablespoons | 6 tablespoons | about 3.3 mg |
| 4 tablespoons | 4 tablespoons | about 6.5 mg |
| 8 tablespoons | none | about 13 mg |

Canadian health officials suggest a first edible dose of 2.5 mg of THC at most. Michigan's limit for one serving of a licensed adult-use edible is 10 mg. Start with no more than about 2.5 mg, which may mean half a cookie, and wait at least 2 hours. For a fuller walkthrough, see our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/).

## Ingredients for one dough, two cookies

The recipe card lists everything: a classic butter, sugar, egg and flour dough, plus chocolate chips for one half and sugar or sprinkles for rolling the other. The one ingredient to plan is the butter. Blend cannabutter and plain butter to your dose, and let both soften to the same temperature so they cream together evenly. You can order flower for a fresh batch of cannabutter ahead from [your local High Society store](/shop/), and earn points with [The Society](/club-member-program/), our free loyalty program.

## Cannabis cookies recipe: one dough, two ways

Cream the butters and sugars for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping the bowl so no streak of cannabutter hides in a corner. After the egg and dry ingredients go in, divide the dough exactly in half and fold the chips into one half. Shape each half into 12 balls, so every cookie gets the same share with or without chips. Bake at 350°F for 9 to 11 minutes, until the edges set but the centers still look soft.

## Mix-in ideas

- Chopped toasted pecans or walnuts
- Dried Michigan tart cherries with white chocolate chips
- A pinch of cinnamon in the rolling sugar
- A dip in melted plain chocolate once they cool

Mix-ins don't change the math as long as the cookie count stays the same. Skip infused chocolate for dipping, though, since it stacks a second dose on top. For a pan bake with the same butter, see our [pot brownies recipe](/blog/pot-brownies-recipe/).

## Storage and labeling

Once cool, the cookies keep in an airtight tin on the counter for up to about a week, or in the freezer for longer. Label the tin "contains THC," with the estimated mg per cookie and the date. An infused cookie looks exactly like a regular one, so keep the tin away from the snack shelf and well beyond kids' and pets' reach. Serve them to guests 21 and older, and tell them first that the cookies are infused.

faq.q: How strong is one cannabis cookie?
faq.a: It depends on your butter and your blend. With cannabutter at about 39 mg per tablespoon at most, 2 tablespoons in this dough works out to roughly 3.3 mg per cookie. The real number is likely lower, since homemade butter loses some THC along the way, but plan servings as if it were the full amount.

faq.q: How long do weed cookies take to kick in?
faq.a: Health Canada gives a range of 30 to 120 minutes, and reaching the full effect can take as long as 4 hours. Effects from edibles can last 4 to 12 hours. That slow start is why people overdo cookies: nothing seems to happen, so they eat another. Start small, give it at least 2 hours, and don't drive.

Yes. Freeze the cooled cookies in a labeled, airtight container with the estimated mg per cookie written on it, and thaw them at room temperature. You can also freeze the dough balls and bake them straight from frozen, adding a minute or two. Keep the frozen stash somewhere kids won't find it.

sources.label: Health Canada: Cannabis, lower your risks
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)
Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency: Technical Bulletin, Maximum THC Concentrations for Marijuana-Infused Products (April 2025, PDF)

ingredients: 8 tablespoons (1/2 cup) butter in total, softened: cannabutter plus plain unsalted butter (see the note)
1/2 cup chocolate chips, for half the dough
2 tablespoons sugar or sprinkles, for rolling the other half
steps: Preheat to 350°F; line two baking sheets with parchment.
Cream the cannabutter, plain butter and both sugars for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping the bowl well.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
In a separate bowl, stir the flour, baking soda and salt, then mix them in until just combined.
Divide the dough in half and fold the chocolate chips into one half.
Shape each half into 12 equal balls. Roll the plain balls in sugar or sprinkles.
Bake for 9 to 11 minutes, until the edges are set. Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
Store airtight, labeled with the estimated mg per cookie.
recipe.dosingNote: An estimate: butter that tops out near 39 mg per tablespoon puts about 78 mg into the dough when you use 2 tablespoons (plus 6 plain), roughly 3.3 mg in each of 24 cookies. Homemade butter usually falls short of its ceiling, since the flower's real potency and the decarb and infusion steps all shave some off. Start with about 2.5 mg or less, half a cookie at this strength, and wait at least 2 hours before considering more. Label the batch and store it well away from kids, pets and the regular cookie jar.

claims.claim: The recipe takes 8 tablespoons of butter and makes about 24 cookies
claims.source: Recipe card: 1/2 cup butter; the dough is split in half and shaped into 12 balls each.

claims.claim: Cannabutter 'tops out near 39 mg per tablespoon, the example from our cannabutter recipe'
claims.fix: 39 mg/tbsp is the full-cup end of that example (630 mg / 16 tbsp); straining out 42 tsp gives 15 mg/tsp = 45 mg/tbsp. Now named as 'the full-cup figure', with a note that butter straining out to less than a cup runs stronger. The table stays keyed to 39 as a stated condition.

claims.claim: Table: 1, 2, 4, 8 tbsp of 39 mg/tbsp butter over 24 cookies = about 1.6, 3.3, 6.5, 13 mg per cookie at most
Canadian health officials suggest a first edible dose of 2.5 mg THC at most
claims.source: Health Canada, Cannabis: lower your risks: 'Look for products that contain 2.5 mg of THC or less'; CCMOH statement (Jan. 6, 2020). Both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Michigan's limit for one serving of a licensed adult-use edible is 10 mg
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-thc-limits (CRA technical bulletin, April 24, 2025: adult-use edibles 10 mg per dose, 200 mg per package).

claims.claim: Start with 'one cookie or half of one' (body); 'Eat one cookie, or half' (dosing note); 'Have one' (FAQ)
claims.fix: One cookie of the article's own example is 3.3 mg, above the 2.5 mg first-dose guidance it cites. Now: start with no more than about 2.5 mg, which may mean half a cookie; FAQ says 'Start small'.
claims.source: Health Canada and CCMOH as above; table arithmetic.

claims.claim: Wait 2 hours before more (dosing note, FAQ)
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours', matching the body.
claims.source: Health Canada: 'It can take up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'.

claims.claim: FAQ: 'For most people, somewhere between 30 and 120 minutes', full effect up to 4 hours
claims.fix: The source gives the range without 'for most people'; now attributed: 'Health Canada gives a range of 30 to 120 minutes'.
claims.source: Health Canada: 'Effects felt within 30 minutes to 2 hours'; 'up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'.

claims.claim: Effects from edibles can last 4 to 12 hours
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'The effects from edible cannabis last 4 to 12 hours'.

claims.source: Standard drop-cookie method; equal counts per half keep the butter share equal with or without chips.

claims.claim: Mix-ins don't change the math if the cookie count stays the same; skip infused chocolate for dipping

Sources resolve and support the text
claims.source: Health Canada and CCMOH opened 2026-10-24. The CRA bulletin is the law-facts source for mi-thc-limits (michigan.gov refuses automated fetches; verified there).

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 15 claims checked, 4 fixed (39 mg attribution, first-serving advice, wait time, 'for most people'). Sources unchanged.
review.writerNotes: No single standard dose presented as right for everyone; the table shows how blending changes the dose. The Society is named as free and point-earning only (no point values or tiers). "Weed cookies" appears only in an FAQ question, per the voice guide. Room-temperature storage of about a week is a quality recommendation, not a sourced shelf life.
